# MCP-as-a-Service

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/README.md

# MCP-as-a-Service


Run MCP servers remotely over HTTP/SSE with on-demand package execution.

`mcp-as-a-service` fetches MCP packages from npm/PyPI, runs them in isolated Podman containers, and exposes them through a web-friendly gateway so clients do not need local stdio runtimes.

Built with Bun + Hono + TypeScript.

## Why This Project

- Centralize MCP runtime execution on infrastructure you control
- Share remote MCP connectivity across many clients
- Start package runtimes only when needed
- Isolate runtimes with Podman security boundaries
- Keep protocol support first-class (`2024-11-05`)

## Best Fit

- Internal MCP gateway for teams
- Hosted MCP runtime for clients that cannot run local processes
- Controlled package execution environment with observability

## Quickstart

Prerequisites:
- Bun 1.1+
- Podman (rootless)

Setup:
```bash
bun install
bun run build:runtime-images
bun run dev
```

Production start:
```bash
bun run start
```

Run tests:
```bash
bun test
```

Default port: `8787` (or `PORT` env var).

## First Success in 60 Seconds

1. Start an SSE stream:
```bash
curl -N "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/firecrawl-mcp/sse?firecrawlApiKey=YOUR_KEY"
```

2. Send a JSON-RPC message:
```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/firecrawl-mcp/messages?firecrawlApiKey=YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0"}}}'
```

## API Overview

Core:
- `GET /` service metadata and usage hints
- `GET /health` health + protocol status
- `GET /servers` active runtime stats

MCP protocol:
- `POST /mcp` JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint
- `GET /mcp/capabilities` server capabilities/status

HTTP/SSE package bridge:
- `GET /package/:packageName/sse` stream server events/messages
- `POST /package/:packageName/messages` send JSON-RPC payloads

Canonical write endpoint is `POST /package/:packageName/messages`.
Removed aliases:
- `POST /package/:packageName/respond`
- `POST /package/:packageName/message`

## Client Usage Example

Claude Desktop:
```bash
claude mcp add firecrawl \
  'https://mcp.llmbase.ai/package/firecrawl-mcp/sse?firecrawlApiKey=YOUR_KEY' \
  -t http
```

Direct MCP:
```bash
curl -X POST https://mcp.llmbase.ai/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0"}}}'
```

## Security and Runtime Model

- Podman-only execution model
- Hardened container defaults (caps dropped, resource limits, isolated network mode)
- Input and argument sanitization
- Parameter-to-env mapping for package configuration
- Automatic cleanup of inactive runtimes

Ubuntu Podman prerequisites:
```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y podman uidmap slirp4netns fuse-overlayfs apparmor apparmor-utils
podman --version
podman info | grep rootless
```

## Current Limits

- In-memory process registry (state resets on restart)
- `maxConcurrentProcesses` default: 10
- Container startup latency depends on package install/bootstrap time

## Architecture

```txt
Client (Claude/Desktop/App)
  -> HTTP/SSE
mcp-as-a-service
  -> JSON-RPC over stdio
Containerized MCP package runtime (npm/pypi)
  -> external APIs/tools/resources
```

## Project Structure

```txt
src/
  app/         app wiring and routes
  transport/   HTTP/SSE and MCP protocol controllers
  runtime/     process orchestration, execution plans, stdio framing
  packages/    package parsing and registry detection
  security/    input and environment policies
  shared/      config, logging, errors, and types
```

## Documentation

- `docs/API_REFERENCE.md` endpoint reference and examples

- `docs/OPERATIONS.md` day-2 operations commands
- `docs/MIGRATION.md` breaking-change migration notes
- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` common failures and fixes

- `docs/CLOUDFLARE_SETUP.md` Cloudflare setup guidance
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` contribution workflow
- `SECURITY.md` vulnerability reporting policy
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` contributor behavior standards

# AGENTS.md

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/AGENTS.md

OBJECTIVE:
This project is an MCP-as-a-Service built on Bun.
It exposes installable Node.js and Python MCP packages over HTTP/SSE.
Packages are fetched and started on demand, then proxied as a remote MCP server API.

TECH STACK:
- Bun Runtime
- Hono.js
- TypeScript
- Podman (runtime isolation)

RUNTIME MODEL:
- Podman-only execution mode.
- Canonical write endpoint: `POST /package/:packageName/messages`.
- SSE endpoint: `GET /package/:packageName/sse`.
- Removed legacy aliases: `/respond` and `/message`.

GUIDELINES:
- Keep it simple.
- Do not overengineer.
- Prefer removing dead code over keeping speculative abstractions.
- Keep docs aligned with actual routes and runtime behavior.

---

# Contributing

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing

Thanks for contributing to `mcp-as-a-service`.

## Development Setup

1. Install Bun.
2. Install Podman (rootless).
3. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   bun install
   ```
4. Build runtime images:
   ```bash
   bun run build:runtime-images
   ```
5. Start in dev mode:
   ```bash
   bun run dev
   ```

## Testing

Run all tests:
```bash
bun test
```

## Code Guidelines

- Keep changes simple and focused.
- Do not overengineer.
- Prefer removing dead code over adding abstraction.
- Preserve podman-only runtime behavior.
- Canonical write endpoint is `/package/:packageName/messages`.

## Pull Requests

- Include a short description of behavior change.
- Include test updates when behavior changes.
- Update docs when endpoints/runtime behavior changes.

# API Reference

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/docs/API_REFERENCE.md

# API Reference

Base URL examples:
- Local: `http://127.0.0.1:8787`
- Production: `https://mcp.llmbase.ai`

## Core Endpoints

### `GET /`
Service metadata, protocol info, and usage hints.

### `GET /health`
Service health.

Example response:
```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "mcp": { "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "initialized": false },
  "execution": { "mode": "podman" }
}
```

### `GET /servers`
Active MCP runtime processes and client counts.

## MCP Protocol

### `POST /mcp`
JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint.

Example:
```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0"}}}'
```

### `GET /mcp/capabilities`
Current MCP capabilities and status.

## HTTP/SSE Proxy

### `GET /package/:packageName/sse`
Start/attach to a package-backed MCP server over SSE.

Example:
```bash
curl -N "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/%40coingecko%2Fcoingecko-mcp/sse?COINGECKO_ENVIRONMENT=demo&COINGECKO_DEMO_API_KEY=test"
```

### `POST /package/:packageName/messages`
Send JSON-RPC payload to the package runtime process.

Example:
```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/%40coingecko%2Fcoingecko-mcp/messages?COINGECKO_ENVIRONMENT=demo&COINGECKO_DEMO_API_KEY=test" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0"}}}'
```

Returns:
```json
{ "accepted": true }
```

## Removed Endpoints

The following legacy aliases were removed and now return `404`:
- `POST /package/:packageName/respond`
- `POST /package/:packageName/message`


---

# Cloudflare Configuration for MCP-as-a-Service

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/docs/CLOUDFLARE_SETUP.md

# Cloudflare Configuration for MCP-as-a-Service

This guide shows how to configure Cloudflare for optimal performance and security with your MCP-as-a-Service deployment.

## 🛡️ Security Rules

### 1. Rate Limiting Rules

Create these rules in **Security > WAF > Rate limiting rules**:

#### Basic API Rate Limiting
```
Rule Name: MCP API Rate Limit
Match: Hostname equals "mcp.llmbase.ai"
Rate: 100 requests per minute per IP
Action: Block for 10 minutes
```

#### Package Endpoint Rate Limiting (More Restrictive)
```
Rule Name: MCP Package Endpoint Rate Limit  
Match: 
  - Hostname equals "mcp.llmbase.ai"
  - URI Path starts with "/package/"
Rate: 20 requests per minute per IP
Action: Block for 5 minutes
```

#### Health Check Exception
```
Rule Name: Health Check Exception
Match:
  - Hostname equals "mcp.llmbase.ai" 
  - URI Path equals "/health"
Action: Skip all remaining rules
```

### 2. Security Level

**Security > Settings**:
- Security Level: `High`
- Challenge Passage: `30 minutes`
- Browser Integrity Check: `Enabled`

### 3. Bot Fight Mode

**Security > Bots**:
- Bot Fight Mode: `Enabled`
- Static Resource Protection: `Enabled`

## 🚀 Performance Optimization

### 1. Caching Rules

**Caching > Caching Rules**:

#### Cache Static Responses
```
Rule Name: Cache API Documentation
Match: URI Path equals "/"
Cache Level: Standard
Edge TTL: 5 minutes
```

#### Don't Cache Package Requests
```
Rule Name: No Cache Package Requests
Match: URI Path starts with "/package/"
Cache Level: Bypass
```

#### Cache Health Checks
```
Rule Name: Cache Health Checks
Match: URI Path equals "/health"
Cache Level: Standard
Edge TTL: 1 minute
```

### 2. Speed Optimization

**Speed > Optimization**:
- Auto Minify: `JavaScript`, `CSS`, `HTML`
- Rocket Loader: `Off` (can break API responses)
- Mirage: `Off`
- Polish: `Off`
- Brotli: `Enabled`

## 🌐 DNS Configuration

**DNS > Records**:

```
Type: A
Name: mcp (or @ for root)
IPv4: YOUR_HETZNER_VPS_IP
Proxy status: Proxied (Orange cloud)
TTL: Auto
```

Optional subdomain:
```
Type: CNAME
Name: api
Target: mcp.llmbase.ai
Proxy status: Proxied
```

## 🔒 SSL/TLS Configuration

**SSL/TLS > Overview**:
- SSL/TLS encryption mode: `Full (strict)`

**SSL/TLS > Edge Certificates**:
- Always Use HTTPS: `Enabled`
- HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS): `Enabled`
  - Max Age Header: `6 months`
  - Include subdomains: `Enabled`
  - No-Sniff header: `Enabled`

## 📊 Analytics & Monitoring

### 1. Analytics

**Analytics > Web Analytics**:
- Enable Web Analytics for detailed traffic insights

### 2. Alerts

**Notifications > Notifications**:
- Rate Limiting Threshold Exceeded
- High Error Rate (4xx/5xx)
- Traffic Spike

## 🔧 Page Rules (Legacy - use Rules engine instead)

If you prefer Page Rules over the new Rules engine:

```
1. mcp.llmbase.ai/health*
   - Cache Level: Standard
   - Edge Cache TTL: 1 minute

2. mcp.llmbase.ai/package/*
   - Cache Level: Bypass
   - Security Level: High

3. mcp.llmbase.ai/*
   - Cache Level: Standard
   - Edge Cache TTL: 5 minutes
   - Security Level: Medium
```

## 🛠️ Advanced Security (Pro/Business Plans)

### 1. Custom Firewall Rules

**Security > WAF > Custom rules**:

#### Block Known Bad Patterns
```javascript
// Block common attack patterns
(http.request.uri.query contains "<?php" or 
 http.request.uri.query contains "<script" or
 http.request.uri.query contains "javascript:" or
 http.request.uri.query contains "vbscript:")
```

#### Geographic Restrictions (if needed)
```javascript
// Allow only specific countries (adjust as needed)
not (ip.geoip.country in {"US" "DE" "GB" "CA" "AU" "FR" "NL" "JP"})
```

### 2. Rate Limiting by Country/ASN

More advanced rate limiting based on:
- Geographic location
- ASN (hosting providers)
- User agent patterns

## 📱 Mobile Optimization

**Speed > Optimization**:
- Accelerated Mobile Pages (AMP): `Off`
- Image Resizing: `Enabled` (Pro+)
- Mirage: `Off` (can interfere with API responses)

## 🔍 Logging & Debugging

### Cloudflare Logpush (Enterprise)

If you have Enterprise plan, configure Logpush to send logs to your preferred destination for analysis.

### Basic Debugging

Use Cloudflare's **Trace** tool:
```bash
curl -H "CF-RAY: on" https://mcp.llmbase.ai/health
```

## 📋 Recommended Cloudflare Plan

For production MCP-as-a-Service:

- **Free**: Basic protection, good for development
- **Pro ($20/month)**: 
  - Advanced DDoS protection
  - Web Analytics
  - Image Optimization
  - Custom Page Rules (20)
- **Business ($200/month)**:
  - Advanced security features
  - Load balancing
  - Custom SSL certificates

## ⚡ Testing Your Setup

After configuration, test your setup:

```bash
# Test rate limiting
for i in {1..25}; do
  curl -w "%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null -s \
    -X POST "https://mcp.llmbase.ai/package/firecrawl-mcp/messages?test=rate$i" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}'
  sleep 1
done

# Test caching
curl -I "https://mcp.llmbase.ai/"
# Look for: cf-cache-status: HIT

# Test security headers
curl -I "https://mcp.llmbase.ai/"
# Look for security headers
```

## 🚨 Monitoring & Alerts

Set up monitoring for:
- Response time increases
- Error rate spikes
- Rate limit triggers
- SSL certificate expiration
- DNS resolution issues

With this Cloudflare configuration, your MCP-as-a-Service will have strong security and performance without application-level rate limiting.

# Deployment Guide

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md

# Deployment Guide

This runbook covers single-host deployment for `mcp-as-a-service` with `systemd --user`.

## Prerequisites

- Ubuntu host with user access (example: `ubuntu@<host>`)
- Bun installed for the service user (`~/.bun/bin/bun`)
- Podman rootless installed and working
- Service checkout at `~/mcp-as-a-service`
- User lingering enabled for reboot persistence:
  ```bash
  sudo loginctl enable-linger ubuntu
  ```

## Deploy Current Workspace to Server

Run from local repo root:

```bash
tar --exclude='.git' --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='combined.log' --exclude='error.log' \
  --exclude='.DS_Store' -czf - AGENTS.md README.md package.json bun.lock tsconfig.json \
  ecosystem.config.cjs src test scripts docs nginx.conf .env.example \
| ssh ubuntu@<host> 'cd ~/mcp-as-a-service && tar -xzf -'
```

## Install and Restart

```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> '
  set -e
  cd ~/mcp-as-a-service
  export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
  bun install
  systemctl --user daemon-reload
  systemctl --user restart mcp-as-a-service.service
  systemctl --user is-active mcp-as-a-service.service
'
```

## Verify

```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8787/health'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8787/servers'
```

Expected:
- service is `active`
- `health.status` is `healthy`
- `execution.mode` is `podman`

## Required Runtime Environment

Service should include:
- `PORT=8787`
- `NODE_ENV=production`
- `PODMAN_READ_ONLY=false` (required for on-the-fly package bootstrap like `npx`)

Check:
```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'systemctl --user show mcp-as-a-service.service -p Environment'
```

## Rollback

If restart fails after deploy:

1. Revert server repo to a known good commit/tag.
2. Reinstall and restart service.

Example:
```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> '
  set -e
  cd ~/mcp-as-a-service
  git log --oneline -n 5
  git checkout <known-good-commit-or-tag>
  export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
  bun install
  systemctl --user restart mcp-as-a-service.service
  curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8787/health
'
```

# MCP Protocol Compliance

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/docs/MCP_COMPLIANCE.md

# MCP Protocol Compliance

This document describes the MCP protocol implementation in `mcp-as-a-service`.

## Overview

The service implements MCP over JSON-RPC 2.0 with protocol version `2024-11-05`.

Implemented areas:
- Protocol version negotiation (`initialize`)
- MCP-compatible error responses
- Capabilities discovery
- Initialization lifecycle (`initialize` -> `notifications/initialized`)

## Protocol Version

- Version: `2024-11-05`
- Source: `src/shared/types/mcp-protocol.ts`

## Endpoints

### MCP JSON-RPC
- `POST /mcp`

Supported methods:
- `initialize`
- `notifications/initialized`
- `capabilities/list`
- `tools/list`
- `resources/list`
- `prompts/list`

### MCP Status Discovery
- `GET /mcp/capabilities`

### HTTP/SSE Proxy Endpoints
- `GET /package/:packageName/sse`
- `POST /package/:packageName/messages`

Removed legacy aliases:
- `POST /package/:packageName/respond`
- `POST /package/:packageName/message`

## Error Codes

### JSON-RPC Standard
- `-32700` Parse error
- `-32600` Invalid request
- `-32601` Method not found
- `-32602` Invalid params
- `-32603` Internal error

### MCP-Specific (`-32000` to `-32099`)
- `-32000` Unsupported protocol version
- `-32001` Resource not found
- `-32002` Resource access denied
- `-32003` Tool not found
- `-32004` Tool execution error
- `-32005` Prompt not found
- `-32006` Server not ready
- `-32007` Capability not supported
- `-32008` Invalid tool arguments
- `-32009` Rate limit exceeded
- `-32010` Timeout error

### Application-Specific MCP Range
- `-32020` Package not found
- `-32021` Runtime not available
- `-32022` Server start failed
- `-32023` Max processes exceeded
- `-32024` Invalid package name
- `-32026` Remote server not supported

Source: `src/shared/errors/error-codes.ts`

## Initialization Flow

1. Client sends `initialize` to `POST /mcp` with `protocolVersion`.
2. Server returns negotiated capabilities and server info.
3. Client sends `notifications/initialized`.
4. Server marks MCP session initialized.

Main implementation: `src/transport/mcp/mcp-controller.ts`.

## Package Metadata

MCP metadata is declared in `package.json` under the `mcp` key:
- protocol version
- server info
- transport endpoints

## Test Coverage

Compliance tests:
- `test/integration/mcp-protocol-compliance.test.ts`

Run:
```bash
bun test test/integration/mcp-protocol-compliance.test.ts
```

Full test suite:
```bash
bun test
```

## Key Implementation Files

- `src/shared/types/mcp-protocol.ts`
- `src/shared/errors/error-codes.ts`
- `src/shared/errors/error-factories.ts`
- `src/transport/mcp/mcp-controller.ts`
- `src/app/routes.ts`

## References

- MCP specification: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/
- JSON-RPC 2.0: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification

# Operations Guide

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/docs/OPERATIONS.md

# Operations Guide

Day-2 commands for running `mcp-as-a-service` in production.

## Service Control

```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'systemctl --user status --no-pager mcp-as-a-service.service'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'systemctl --user restart mcp-as-a-service.service'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'systemctl --user stop mcp-as-a-service.service'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'systemctl --user start mcp-as-a-service.service'
```

## Logs

```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'journalctl --user -u mcp-as-a-service.service -n 100 --no-pager'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'tail -n 100 ~/mcp-as-a-service/combined.log'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'tail -n 100 ~/mcp-as-a-service/error.log'
```

## Health and Smoke Checks

```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8787/health'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8787/servers'
```

CoinGecko SSE smoke test:
```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'timeout 10 curl -sS -N \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/%40coingecko%2Fcoingecko-mcp/sse?COINGECKO_ENVIRONMENT=demo&COINGECKO_DEMO_API_KEY=test" \
  | sed -n "1,8p"'
```

Expected first event:
- `event: status`
- `data: {"type":"connected", ...}`

## API Surface Checks

Canonical endpoint:
```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/firecrawl-mcp/messages" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"ping\"}"'
```

Removed aliases should return `404`:
```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/firecrawl-mcp/respond" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{}"'
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8787/package/firecrawl-mcp/message" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{}"'
```

## Persistence

Ensure lingering is enabled:
```bash
ssh ubuntu@<host> 'loginctl show-user ubuntu -p Linger'
```

Expected:
- `Linger=yes`

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md

# Troubleshooting

## Service does not start

Check:
```bash
systemctl --user status --no-pager mcp-as-a-service.service
journalctl --user -u mcp-as-a-service.service -n 100 --no-pager
```

Common fixes:
- Bun not in PATH for service user
- wrong working directory in service file
- syntax/runtime error in current build

## `RUNTIME_NOT_AVAILABLE` / Podman missing

Verify:
```bash
podman --version
podman info | grep rootless
```

Install (Ubuntu):
```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y podman uidmap slirp4netns fuse-overlayfs apparmor apparmor-utils
```

## Package starts then exits quickly

Likely causes:
- missing required API key/environment parameter
- package-specific startup error
- runtime cannot write cache/temp during bootstrap

Checks:
```bash
tail -n 200 ~/mcp-as-a-service/combined.log
tail -n 200 ~/mcp-as-a-service/error.log
```

For dynamic `npx` bootstrapping, ensure service has:
- `PODMAN_READ_ONLY=false`

## `PACKAGE_NOT_FOUND`

The package name was not found in npm or PyPI.

Check:
- spelling / scope encoding
- package exists publicly
- no remote URL passed as package name

## Remote URL rejected (`REMOTE_SERVER_NOT_SUPPORTED`)

This service accepts installable package names, not remote MCP server URLs.

Use:
- npm/pypi package names via `/package/:packageName/sse` or `/messages`

## Removed endpoints returning 404

Expected behavior:
- `/package/:packageName/respond` -> `404`
- `/package/:packageName/message` -> `404`

Use:
- `POST /package/:packageName/messages`

## Service not persistent after reboot

Enable lingering:
```bash
sudo loginctl enable-linger ubuntu
loginctl show-user ubuntu -p Linger
```

# Security Policy

Source: https://github.com/llmbaseai/mcp-hosting/blob/main/SECURITY.md

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

This project is pre-1.0.0. Security fixes are applied on the latest `main` branch.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Please do not open public issues for undisclosed vulnerabilities.

Report by email to: `support@llmbase.ai` (replace with your actual security contact).

Include:
- Vulnerability description
- Reproduction steps
- Impact assessment
- Suggested remediation (if known)

## Security Notes

- Runtime execution is podman-only.
- Remote MCP URLs are rejected; only installable npm/pypi packages are accepted.
- Do not place API keys in committed files.

---
